photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of a named Potawatomi councillor ("The Sucker") in traditional dress—turban, cloth shirt, leggings, moccasins, blanket—holding a pipe, documenting Potawatomi dress and material culture.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard; photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio portrait of a Potawatomi man in regalia (roach, shell gorget, fringed shirt, quillwork armbands, beaded bandolier) for a Hiawatha play; despite the theatrical context, the clothing and adornment are genuine Native-made items documenting Potawatomi dress, so this is a documentary photo of dress belonging to the claimed people.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of a named Potawatomi chief, Thunder Coming Down to the Ground, wearing a blanket, shirt, jacket, trousers and shoes, documenting Native dress in the 19th century.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: This is a documentary studio portrait of White Bear (Se-nadz-win), identified as a Potawatomi chief, in period clothing; such a photograph of a named individual from this people fits the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Wa-wa-suk, identified as a Potawatomi councillor, documenting his dress and presence in Washington DC; a documentary photo of the named people's member fits the claim.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard; photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio portrait of a Potawatomi woman wearing beaded headband, necklaces, bracelets and a fringed hide dress — actual Native-made regalia, even if posed for a "Hiawatha" stage costume — which counts as a documentary photo of dress within the allowed genres.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of a named Potawatomi chief wearing a blanket over a suit, documenting his dress and identity; this is a legitimate documentary photo of the claimed people.

household.name: Prescription stick
household.title: Prescription Stick
household.reason: A wooden stick incised with pictographic rows of trees and figures, identified as a Prairie Potawatomi "prescription stick" (a mnemonic device used by a medicine practitioner), a genuine traditional household/utility object of this people.

arms.name: Staff
arms.title: Staff
arms.reason: This is a carved wooden dance/war staff with a human face finial, deer dewclaw rattles, and hide wrappings—a documented Potawatomi/Great Lakes ceremonial object type, consistent with the claimed maker and period.
